where: Section 3, worked example step 6, table, and exam trap 1 (Bredt on the angle)
problem: The perimeter is wrong. With a centre-line side of 58 mm the perimeter is 4 × 58 = 232 mm, not 240 mm. Every closed-box number built on s = 240 (J = 377 217 mm⁴, θ = 0.0393 rad = 2.25°, the 1180 stiffness ratio, 14.86 MPa curve) inherits the error.
fix: Use s = 232 mm: J = 4 × 3364² × 2 / 232 = 390 224 mm⁴; θ = 4 × 10⁸ / (27 000 × 390 224) = 0.0380 rad = 2.18°; stiffness ratio 390 224 / 320 = 1219; τ = T/(2At) = 14.9 N/mm² is unchanged. Update the table, the text 'about 1180' to 'about 1220', and exam trap 1 to read 390 224 mm⁴ instead of 377 217 mm⁴.

problem: The statement 'Two silent factors of 1000 turn 46 rad into 46 mrad' is wrong. The two factors cancel: skipping both conversions gives 200 × 2000 / (27 × 320) = 46.3, the right number by accident. One factor gives 46 296 rad (G left in GPa) or 46.3 mrad (T left in N·m), not two.
fix: Write: leaving G in GPa makes θ 1000 times too large (46 296 rad instead of 46.3 rad); leaving T in N·m makes it 1000 times too small (0.0463 rad = 46.3 mrad). Make both slips and the errors cancel, so the answer looks right in the wrong units — always convert to N, mm, N/mm² before dividing.

where: Section 3 opening sentence and worked example parts (a) and (b)
problem: 'The same 240 mm of 2 mm strip that a 60 mm × 60 mm angle uses' is wrong. The angle has two legs of 60 mm along the centre line, so it uses about 120 mm of strip (about 118 mm developed), and step 1 itself adds only 60 + 60 = 120 mm. The closed box therefore uses roughly twice the material of the angle, so the claim that the comparison is 'from identical material' is false.
fix: Either state plainly that the box uses about twice the strip length of the angle, or keep the material identical: from 120 mm of strip make a box with mean side 30 mm, A = 900 mm², s = 120 mm, J = 4 × 900² × 2/120 = 54 000 mm⁴; then θ = 4 × 10⁸ / (27 000 × 54 000) = 0.274 rad (15.7°), τ = 200 000 / (2 × 900 × 2) = 55.6 N/mm², and the box is about 169 times stiffer than the open angle.

problem: 'The same 200 mm of 3 mm strip' is not the same strip as in Q4, where the strip is 100 mm wide and 3 mm thick. A student may think the 200 mm is the 100 mm width of Q4.
fix: Write 'A 200 mm length of the same 3 mm strip (twice the material of Q4) is closed into a square box with mean side 50 mm', and note that the 417× stiffness gain is at equal torque, not at equal material.
